question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund projects FCFF for year 6 (T+1) of INR 200 crore for investee Gamma Ltd. WACC is 12%, terminal growth rate is 5%. What is the terminal value at end of year 5?

explanation.text: The Logic: TV = FCF(T+1) / (WACC - g) = 200 / (0.12 - 0.05) = 200 / 0.07 = INR 2,857.14 crore. This is the Gordon growth formula used in Step 2 of the DCF illustration (Example 12.5). The Trap: INR 1,666.67 uses FCF/WACC (ignores growth). INR 4,000 uses WACC+g in denominator. INR 1,400 divides by (WACC+g) incorrectly. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XXI-B (Portfolio Manager), XV all test Gordon TV. X-B applies for business valuation. Manager's Pro-Tip: In Cat III event-driven desks running 'SOTP DCF' on demerger targets, use different terminal growth per business line - a consumer unit at 6% and a cyclical unit at 3% avoids the single-g trap.
